title: Pixels, tensors and shapes
hook: Why IMAGE is [B, H, W, C] and LATENT is [B, C, H/8, W/8], what the VAE nodes do to cross between them, and where truncating 8-bit levels bites.

verified.claim: IMAGE is [B, H, W, C] and LATENT samples are [B, C, H/8, W/8], with EmptyLatentImage building zeros of that shape.
VAE encode crops, moves the axis and rescales, and decode reverses that with a clamp.
SaveImage multiplies by 255, clips and casts to uint8, which truncates.
Layout, crop, clamp and 8-bit results come from running PyTorch on CPU, with the arithmetic copied from these functions.
The two graphs pass validate_prompt and ran on a CPU.
Float formats and their bit counts follow Kalamkar et al. 2019, Table 1, and torch.finfo agrees with the eps printed in the lab.

unchecked: The lab works on a clean ramp of values, not on a real VAE's output, and it measures no visible loss.
